match.reason: The closest bank point, bus-profit, covers revenue and expenses mainly as parts of profit and risk, whereas the new point defines them by their effect on owner's equity, which is a different idea and not just a small change.

draft.title: Revenue and expenses
card: an inflow that increases owner's equity, such as fees earned or sales. It comes from the business's normal activities.
an outflow that decreases owner's equity, such as wages, rent or electricity. It is the cost of running the business.
Revenue is recorded when it is earned, even if the cash has not yet arrived. Owner's equity rises when revenue is earned and falls when an expense is incurred.
The owner putting in more money is not revenue, and the owner taking money out is not an expense. These change equity in a different way.
draft.remember: Revenue increases owner's equity. Expenses decrease it.

a.q: Which item is an expense for a business?
opts: Wages paid to a staff member
Fees earned from a client
Cash put in by the owner
Sales made to a customer
a.why: Wages are an outflow that decreases owner's equity, so they are an expense. Cash put in by the owner is tempting because it involves money, but it is not an expense or revenue, and it does not come from running the business.
a.clue: Which one is a cost of running the business?

b.q: Priya runs a tutoring business in Geelong. She tutors a student in June and sends a bill for the fee. The student pays in July. When does Priya earn the revenue?
opts: In June, when she does the tutoring
In July, when the student pays
In June, when she buys her pens
When Priya next puts money in
b.why: Revenue is recorded when it is earned, even if the cash has not yet arrived. Priya earned the fee when she tutored in June. July is tempting because that is when the cash comes in, but the card says cash does not need to arrive first.
b.clue: Revenue is recorded when it is earned, not when paid.

a.best: Wages paid to a staff member

b.best: In June, when she does the tutoring

problems.detail: The clue says 'Revenue is recorded when it is earned, not when paid', which rules out July. With July gone, the June tutoring option is the only plausible answer left, so the clue gives the answer away.

Two distractors are implausible ('When Priya next puts money in' and 'In June, when she buys her pens'), so the only real choice is between the two plausible options, June tutoring and July payment. That makes the question too easy to test the earned-versus-received idea.
